name: Bradbury Landing
summary: The first ground Curiosity stood on, on the floor of Gale between the northern rim and the mound at its centre.
finding: Where Curiosity touched down in August 2012. First record of NASA’s waypoint file.

evidence.text: Where Curiosity touched down in August 2012. First record of NASA’s waypoint file.

sources: NASA waypoint file, first record (sol 3, RMC 2_0)

name: Cumberland drill hole
imageAlt: NASA drill-site image: Cumberland drill hole
imageSource: Delivered original Cumberland Drilling details.png (1920x1080), NASA/JPL-Caltech/MSSS
summary: The second hole Curiosity drilled, a few metres from John Klein in the Sheepbed mudstone at Yellowknife Bay.
finding: First drilled sample. Mudstone interpreted as a shallow-lake deposit; the samples contain clay minerals and sulfate salts alongside detrital basaltic minerals.
geologicalContext: Unit: Sheepbed member, Yellowknife Bay formation.

evidence.text: Second drilled sample, a few metres from John Klein.

sources: Drill sol: Curiosity drill-attempt table (PMC8981195, Table 3) / NASA image captions

imageSource: Delivered original Windjana Drilling details.png (1917x1078), NASA/JPL-Caltech/MSSS
summary: A hole drilled into a sandstone outcrop at the Kimberley, on the crater floor.
finding: Sandstone outcrop on the crater floor; third drilled sample.

evidence.text: Sandstone outcrop on the crater floor; third drilled sample.

sources: Drill sol: Curiosity drill-attempt table (PMC8981195, Table 3) / NASA image captions

name: Confidence Hills, Pahrump Hills
unit: Murray formation (base of the Mount Sharp group)
summary: The first sample of the Murray formation, where Curiosity reached the base of the Mount Sharp strata.
finding: Where Curiosity first reached Mount Sharp strata; first sample of the Murray formation.
geologicalContext: Unit: Murray formation (base of the Mount Sharp group).

name: Vera Rubin Ridge
summary: The start of the ridge campaign, on terrain picked out from orbit by its hematite signature.

evidence.text: The start of the ridge campaign, on terrain picked out from orbit by its hematite signature.

sources: Curiosity drill-attempt table (PMC8981195, Table 3) and NASA image captions, via the project landmark registry

name: Aberlady, Glen Torridon
summary: The first drill site in Glen Torridon, the region with the strongest clay signature from orbit.
finding: First drill site in Glen Torridon, the region with the strongest clay signature from orbit. The campaign (January 2019 – January 2021) covered about 5 km and 11 drill holes and found the highest clay abundances of the mission.

evidence.text: First drill site in Glen Torridon, the region with the strongest clay signature from orbit. The campaign (January 2019 – January 2021) covered about 5 km and 11 drill holes and found the highest clay abundances of the mission.

sources: Drill sol: Curiosity drill-attempt table (PMC8981195, Table 3) / NASA image captions; Bennett et al. 2023, doi:10.1029/2022JE007185

name: Mont Mercou cliff face
summary: A cliff of bedded sedimentary rock about six metres high, profiled from several angles before the rover climbed it.
finding: The bedding exposed in the cliff records how these sedimentary rocks were laid down.
geologicalContext: The team circled the base to image the outcrop at different viewing geometries and illuminations, mapping its structures, then drilled at the top as a companion to the Nontron drill at its base.

evidence.text: A cliff of bedded sedimentary rock about six metres high, profiled from several angles before the rover climbed it.

sources: NASA Mars Science Laboratory mission blog, sols 3074-3089

name: Greenheugh Pediment caprock
summary: The rocks that cap the pediment: a different formation from the sedimentary layers that built the mountain below.
finding: A geological contact between the mountain strata and the unit that caps the pediment.
geologicalContext: The rover studied the sedimentary rocks below before driving up to the edge of the capping rocks.

evidence.text: The rocks that cap the pediment: a different formation from the sedimentary layers that built the mountain below.

sources: NASA Mars Science Laboratory mission blog, sols 3396-3397

name: Paraitepuy Pass buttes
summary: Towering buttes and exposed layers on either side of a narrow pass, reached by picking a route over ripples and around boulders.
finding: The buttes expose the layering the team had been driving towards for years.
geologicalContext: The pass is guarded by large ripples and several large boulders; the drive threaded between them.

evidence.text: Towering buttes and exposed layers on either side of a narrow pass, reached by picking a route over ripples and around boulders.

sources: NASA Mars Science Laboratory mission blog, sol 3565
